findings.reason: The protected solution is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. Its minimal documented Node model makes the app contract self-contained, while current, following, normal_gap, wrap_gap, and node expose the traversal and splice roles without auxiliary collections or unnecessary helpers.

A value between a non-descending adjacent pair can be inserted directly without violating either inequality. At the sole maximum-to-minimum wrap, a new extreme belongs when it is at least the maximum side or at most the minimum side. If neither predicate succeeds during a full cycle, any link is valid. The two-link splice inserts exactly one node, preserves the original nodes and circularity, and returns the supplied head for every nonempty input; the empty case creates the required self-cycle.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 708, Python, and the native insert(head, insertVal) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms that the supplied node may be any cycle position, multiple insertion locations may be valid, a nonempty call must return the original supplied node, and an empty call must return a newly created one-node cycle.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065629085 use the same empty-list construction, one-cycle traversal, normal-gap and wrap-gap predicates, full-cycle fallback, two-link splice, and original-head return. Their only structural differences are the required app-local Node model and solve function versus LeetCode's injected Node and Solution.insert wrapper.

The unchanged three authored workloads grow increasing circular lists from 32 to 400 nodes with the supplied head at the minimum and a new maximum, forcing the protected algorithm to reach the final wrap once. In a fresh real-test run, the exact protected source passed all twelve ordinary cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent +0.01 and a 1.02x largest runtime ratio. A correct control that restarts from head for every possible gap passed every output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +1.05 and a 70.98x largest runtime ratio, distinguishing one linear cycle from quadratic repeated prefix walks.

The Approach accurately distinguishes ordinary and wrap gaps, bounds traversal to one cycle, explains the uniform-list fallback, details the constant-space splice, and proves preservation of cyclic sorted order. Its O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The four-section modular Reference covers arbitrary-head circular order, empty and one-node insertion, duplicate placements, extreme values across the wrap, original linked-list head return, and preservation of circular links. Its explicit linked-list return type keeps the dynamic contract serializing circular node results correctly. Two independently authored accessible Mermaid cycles preserve the source's before-and-after Example 1 diagrams without copying provider assets.

The authenticated live Premium statement directly verified exactly three examples in source order, explanations on the first two only, two source diagrams and no tables, an arbitrary supplied node in non-descending cyclic order, any order-preserving insertion location, original-node return for nonempty input, self-cycling allocation for empty input, 0 to 50000 nodes, and values from -1000000 through 1000000. The hash-bound source_fidelity.json validates as verified with statement content SHA-256 21ffd2538e1959a4f4b636f161c6d3ea20e8df0aed3986d885acc0c2bcc8d90b.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly three examples. Their exact cycle encodings, insertion values, and outputs remain first and in source order; the first two include source explanations and the third does not.

All twelve ordinary correctness checks are visible samples or trials. The former hidden uniform-cycle, duplicate-insertion, and rotated-head behaviors were exposed, so cases.json no longer conceals any correctness behavior.

Contract boundaries cover an empty cycle, a one-node cycle, insertion and node values at -1000000 and 1000000, a supplied head above the minimum, and original-head traversal order. A legal 50000-node maximum-length cycle was checked separately without bloating an ordinary case; persisted benchmark tiers cover scaling behavior.

Material behavior covers ordinary gaps, the maximum-to-minimum wrap, new minima and maxima, equal insertion values, a distinct insertion into a uniform cycle, duplicate values, and several valid insertion locations.

Expected results and structure were checked across 32347 exhaustive empty or cyclically sorted inputs with every head rotation, lengths through seven, values from -2 through 2, and insertion values from -3 through 3, plus 300 deterministic random cycles. A separate 50000-node boundary check verified the exact app and immutable native algorithms preserve every original node, add exactly one node, return the original nonempty head, close the cycle, retain the required multiset, and leave at most one cyclic descent.

Every case uses a structural circular-insertion validator, so alternate placements allowed by the source contract are accepted instead of being compared to one arbitrary serialized answer. The unchanged 32, 128, and 400-node workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, span 12.5x, and make the correct quadratic control fail only the scaling verdict.
